foundByDrivingTheRealSurfaceNotByReading.finding: G-135's unmeasured thing is measured: on an authenticated full-shell bastrop_tx session the map iframe MOUNTS AND RENDERS. #map-site src=/property-map.html?cityKey=bastrop_tx, stage hidden=false, frame box 378x200; inside the frame #pm-map carries `leaflet-container`, 6 of 6 tile images loaded, and 12 /api/property-map/(layers) responses came FROM the mounted frame, 0 of them non-200. The paragraph in G-135 that said this 'has never once happened' is now false, in the direction it wanted.
foundByDrivingTheRealSurfaceNotByReading.how: scripts/full-shell-probe.mjs, four passes (bare visit, /?cityKey=bastrop_tx, /?lens=fleet, /?lens=police) against https://app.smartcityos.io with the lane-verification key seeded into the product's own hauska_key localStorage slot by an init script, so the app's own x-hauska-key path is what authenticates.

foundByDrivingTheRealSurfaceNotByReading.finding: THE MAP PAGE'S OWN ADDRESS CONTROLS ARE HIDDEN INSIDE THE SHELL, BY THE MAP PAGE'S OWN CODE. web/property-map.js adds `pm-embedded` to the frame's <body> when `window.self !== window.top`; web/property-map.css hides `.pm-search` and `.pm-status` under that class. Measured in the mounted frame: embedded=true, computed display of the search form = none, of the status line = none, and the page's own Search button measures 0x0. So a pointer cannot drive the frame's search inside the shell -- not because the driver was impatient (three rungs of a ladder failed before this was read at source) but because the page does not offer the control. Driving the page's OWN control events inside the frame makes the page's OWN search() fire its OWN fetch: 1 /api/property-map/summary request came FROM the frame (http 200) and the frame's own render targets moved to 'Matched: 908 PINE ST, BASTROP, TX, 78602', parcel 34137. The shell separately reads the same route for its own dock (web/app.js loadPropertyDock, G-128) from the TOP frame; both readings are recorded, and which frame made which request is part of the artifact.
foundByDrivingTheRealSurfaceNotByReading.whyItMattersForTheNextReader: A probe that reported 'the map search does not settle inside the shell' without this would be reporting a defect in the product that is a design decision, and would invite a 'fix' that re-adds a second search box inside an embedded page whose shell already has one.

foundByDrivingTheRealSurfaceNotByReading.finding: THIS LANE'S OWN PROBE LIED TWICE BEFORE IT TOLD THE TRUTH, and both lies are recorded rather than tidied away. (a) Runs 1-3 swallowed the driver's failures in `.catch(() => {})`, so an unreachable field and a search that never ran produced the same artifact: nothing. From run 2 every gesture's outcome is recorded with its own error. (b) Run 4 reported the last rung `ok: true` because `requestSubmit()` did not throw -- while NO request ever reached the wire, because the fill's value had not survived and the page's handler read an empty field and returned early. The rung is now believed only when a /api/property-map/summary request arrives FROM THE FRAME, within a bounded wait. 'The gesture returned' is not 'the page searched'.
foundByDrivingTheRealSurfaceNotByReading.whyItMatters: It is the same class as the dormant mechanism this lane was sent to fix: a check that reports success while measuring nothing is worse than no check, because it closes the question.

foundByDrivingTheRealSurfaceNotByReading.finding: A REGION COULD PRINT 'is generating records' OVER A BASIS LISTING REFUSALS. Adding the live-path refusal status exposed a fall-through in web/app.js's regionHead: any status that was not one of the seam's four fell through to the ok head sentence. `unavailable` (a read that did not succeed) and `refused` (a read that succeeded and whose records failed the shape) shared one kicker and one head. They are now two words, two heads, and the fall-through is unreachable by any payload this product produces -- asserted by a test that gives every state a distinct kicker and a distinct head.
foundByDrivingTheRealSurfaceNotByReading.how: Read the rendered sentence path after wiring `refused`, not the status vocabulary alone; the defect was in the sentence, not the state.

foundByDrivingTheRealSurfaceNotByReading.finding: THE PRE-LANE INSTRUMENT FAILS ON A RECAPTURED NAMESPACE, WHICH IS THE SECOND HALF OF THE NAMED TRAP AND WAS NOT OBVIOUS FROM THE DISPATCH. Run against the same synthetic recapture the fixed instrument passes, HEAD's check.mjs REFUSES A VERDICT (exit 2) because its own self-test fixtures are bare-form (`OPR-03`) and a namespace recapture makes them stale: the instrument reports 'SELF-TEST FAILED: operator: accepts the declared format' and never reaches the boards. So the trap has two distinct failure surfaces -- the truncating extractor (a false accusation against a good board) and the stale fixture (a refusal to speak) -- and both are now cases in the fleet violation suite with their expected exits.
foundByDrivingTheRealSurfaceNotByReading.how: The suite reads HEAD's check.mjs with `git show HEAD:_design/smartcity-fleet-lens/check.mjs` and runs the recapture through it, rather than asserting from memory what the old instrument would have done.

leave_behind: THE PROBE'S TWO SELF-LIES ARE THE MOST TRANSFERABLE THING IN THIS FILE. A driver that swallows its own exceptions and a gesture that is believed because it did not throw both produce green artifacts over nothing measured. Any future browser probe in this program should carry the same two rules this one now has: every gesture records its own outcome, and a search is believed only when the request arrives from the frame that was driven.

ANYONE RE-PROBING THE MAP IFRAME INSIDE THE SHELL: the address controls are hidden by the map page's own embedded rule (pm-embedded). Do not read that as a defect and do not re-add a search box inside the embedded page -- the shell has its own property path (G-128) and reads it from the top frame.

THE LIVE REGIONS ON BASTROP WILL READ `refused` ONCE THIS BRANCH IS DEPLOYED, and that is the acceptance wording rather than a regression: every live record fails its declared shape today (102 of 102), and the mapping -- engine state onto declared bands, a band from the raw reading, an operator identity from the platform route -- is the next unit of work.
